g.text: Turnout change by political balance, weighted
Each dot is one Israeli locality: its 2022 vote balance between the Netanyahu coalition and the opposition (left–right),
and how much its turnout changed from 2022 to 2026 (up–down). Bars: each group's mean weighted by eligible voters; shading: 95% CI.
Coalition: Likud, Religious Zionism, Shas, United Torah Judaism. Opposition: Yesh Atid, National Unity, Yisrael Beiteinu, Labor, Meretz. Arab-party and other votes are excluded from the balance.

Gray: an Arab party (Ra'am, Hadash–Ta'al or Balad) was the single most-voted list in 2022; horizontal position in that panel carries no meaning. Turnout = votes ÷ eligible voters at the locality's ballot boxes
(double envelopes excluded). Sources: Central Elections Committee 2022 final results; CEC 2026 results by locality, all boxes counted (31 Oct 2026, not yet certified). n = 1,215 localities.
Weights: 2022 eligible voters; the CI uses the effective number of localities, (Σw)² ÷ Σw². All localities combined = Σ votes ÷ Σ eligible voters in each year.
